name: Encorafenib + Binimetinib (BRAF/MEK inhibitor, BRAF V600 melanoma)

biomarkers.note: BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination REQUIRES a BRAF V600 activating mutation. Studied in unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600-mutant melanoma (COLUMBUS: treatment-naive or progressed on/after first-line immunotherapy). Do NOT use in BRAF wild-type disease. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous.

lineOfTherapy: BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy for unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600-mutant melanoma (COLUMBUS: first-line, or after prior first-line immunotherapy)

supportiveCare: Baseline and periodic LVEF (echocardiogram) for MEK-inhibitor cardiomyopathy; ophthalmologic assessment for serous retinopathy/retinal vein occlusion; dermatologic surveillance for secondary cutaneous malignancy.

Monitor for MEK/BRAF-inhibitor toxicities (rash, elevated CK/myopathy, hepatotoxicity, venous thromboembolism) per Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 21 (MS-66 onward). Encorafenib/binimetinib is generally associated with a lower rate of pyrexia than dabrafenib/trametinib.

monitoring: ophthalmologic assessment (serous retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion)
LFTs, creatine kinase, CBC; clinical/radiographic response assessment

doseModificationRules.condition: decline in LVEF, serous retinopathy, or grade 3 to 4 toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or reduce per labeling for symptomatic/significant LVEF decline, retinal events, elevated CK/myopathy, or grade 3 to 4 toxicity; obtain clinical review.
